title: [RFE] [Openconnect] nm plasma applet should support PKCS11 usercerts
line: OpenConnect VPN settings can now use a user certificate stored on a smart card or security token, picked from a list or kept when saving.
explanation: The OpenConnect editor treated the user certificate and key fields as local file paths only. A PKCS#11 URI (pkcs11:...) set up elsewhere, for example with nm-connection-editor, was shown but saved back as an empty string, so editing the connection in Plasma silently removed the certificate, and there was no way to choose a certificate from a token. The change stores pkcs11: URIs in the certificate and key fields unchanged, and adds a button next to User Certificate that lists the certificates found on smart cards and tokens (through p11-kit, skipping the system trust store) and fills in its URI; OpenConnect then finds the private key on the same token and asks for its PIN when connecting.

commits.message:
openconnect: allow user certificates from smart cards and tokens

The editor turned PKCS#11 certificate URIs into empty paths on saving,
and had no way to pick a certificate stored on a smart card or token.
Keep pkcs11: URIs as they are and add a button that lists token certs.

BUG: 514263

media.caption: Connection with a token certificate after changing an unrelated option and saving: the User Certificate is gone (NetworkManager now has usercert='').
Same steps with the fix: the pkcs11: URI is still there after saving and reopening, stored unchanged.
User Certificate only offers a file chooser.
New token button next to User Certificate lists the certificates on the security token.
Connecting with the token certificate already asked for the token PIN on master.
Still the same with the fix: the PIN prompt appears and the certificate loads.

review.text: The widget-editor part is sound: keeping pkcs11: URIs stops real data loss, and the p11-kit picker (optional dependency, trust modules skipped) works and is well verified on a SoftHSM token. But the OpenConnect editor was just ported to QML (808aae0b2, libs/editorqml, actively developed toward replacing the widget KCM) and its pathToUrl/urlToPath round-trip drops pkcs11: URIs the same way, so the bug comes back as soon as that editor ships. The token scan also loads and initialises every PKCS#11 module synchronously on the GUI thread, which can freeze the KCM on slow or unplugged readers.
changes: Apply the same pkcs11: URI preservation in libs/editorqml/settings/vpn/openconnect/openconnectsetting.cpp (pathToUrl/urlToPath for usercert, userkey, mcacert, mcakey), ideally with the token picker exposed there too through a small shared helper.
Run the p11-kit token enumeration off the GUI thread (e.g. QtConcurrent) or at least show a busy cursor while it runs.
